text:
elyse: Heads-up: after merging kernel-autotune v3 we see an ~18% p95 latency increase on short-seq workloads. Repro on staging.

jordan: Can you paste the perf trace? which kernel was the autotuner choosing for seqlen <= 32?

elyse: Uploading the profiler excerpt. Looks like autotuner picks 'matmul_packed_v2' for short seq, but launch overhead is up ~0.9ms vs matmul_fast at ~0.3ms when batch size < 6.

ravi: @elyse can you share the nsys timeline dump? might be CUDA stream / launch latency noise.

elyse: Here's the short excerpt from nsys (filtered):
```
2026-03-16 14:07:12 PROFILE: kernel=matmul_packed_v2 launch=0.92ms exec=0.12ms total=1.04ms
2026-03-16 14:07:12 PROFILE: kernel=matmul_fast launch=0.28ms exec=0.18ms total=0.46ms
batch=4 seqlen=16 kv_hit=true
```

mike: Interesting — matmul_packed_v2 gives better throughput at big batches but has a large fixed launch cost. Autotune probably compared peak TFLOPS / throughput numbers, not per-request p95.

sam: We saw the same pattern with continuous batching: when KV cache hits reduce seq length, many tiny batches form; scheduler picks the high-throughput kernel and latency suffers.

ravi: Proposed quick fix: add a seq-length-aware penalty term in the autotuner objective so for seqlen <= 32 prefer low-launch-cost kernels. Also add sticky kernel affinity for routes with high KV hit rate to reduce kernel switch thrash.

jordan: Sounds sensible. Another lever is to make the batcher prefer merging small inflight requests up to a minimum batch size before dispatch (if latency SLO allows). That trades some throughput for better p95.

elyse: I'll run an A/B: autotune-v3 + seq-penalty vs autotune-v2 baseline. Hypothesis: p95 drops significantly on short-seq traffic, throughput on long sequences might drop a bit. Planning a canary tomorrow.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: canary autopick-v3 -> 3 nodes in us-west applied :white_check_mark:

mike: For the AB, include a KV-hit filter in metrics and measure kernel switch rate per route — we suspect frequent kernel switching causes cache fragmentation and extra copy/params setup costs.

sam: :eyes: I'll add a lightweight metric 'kernel_sticky_ratio' to Console (per-route) and emit it for the canary.

elyse: Thanks — experiment steps / commands I'm using:
```
# profile
nsys profile -o run1 --sample=all --trace=cuda python -m inference.bench --model small --seqlen 16 --batch 4
# autotune run
python infra/autotune/run.py --metrics perf.json --seq-penalty 0.15
```

jordan: If the AB looks good we should surface the seq-aware suggestion in Redwood Optimize so customers get it as a recommendation.

elyse: :thumbsup: will post results later today.
